stock_segments.discussion_summary: Peter from Kavalier discusses Revolution Race, which has seen the share price drop due to lowered long-term targets and concerns about major owners Altor and Nyrenstein potentially selling shares. Despite this, Peter sees strong fundamentals with high gross margins >70%, 20% expected growth, and attractive valuation at P16.5. He views any potential drop as a buying opportunity, noting that after previous placements the stock has risen strongly. The hosts find it interesting but don't make a clear recommendation.

stock_segments.discussion_summary: The hosts discuss their case study of Bergman & Beving, which they bought at around 80-95 SEK (P10.2) and sold at 115 SEK. The stock has since soared to 282 SEK (P39), a 250% increase from when they first discussed it. Despite declining earnings per share (-8%) due to higher interest expenses, the stock's valuation has exploded from P10 to P39, far above historical averages. The explanation is that Bergman & Beving has moved from being seen as an ugly series of acquirers to being included in the "fine series" with companies like Lagercrantz, Adtech, and Indutrade trading at P35-41. The hosts find it fascinating and difficult to understand how valuation can change so dramatically when a company moves between market segments.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Det är fascinerande. När man flyttar mellan facken, börsen börjar se något helt annat än man sett tidigare.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Från 10 i PE till 39 i PE på två år. Det är skyhögt över historiska värderingen. Börsdata är ungefär 17,5 på tioårsnitt.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Vi hittar ingen mos i några av de här bolagen. Mården och safety det går inte. Vi förstår inte riktigt varför det ska vara P40 på de här.

bear_case: Extremely high valuation at P39 vs historical 17.5

Interest expenses eating 30% of operating result
catalysts: Continued inclusion in quality trading group

risks: Valuation may revert to historical averages

stock_segments.discussion_summary: The hosts provide a detailed update on Loomis, discussing their shift in strategy regarding Loomis Pay from unrealistic growth targets (5 billion SEK by 2025) to more realistic break-even targets for 2026-2027. Q4 and Q1 reports both came in as expected with organic growth just above 6% and margins in line with previous years. However, the stock reacted differently - up 8% on Q4 report, down 8% on Q1 report. The hosts are puzzled by weak EBITDA margins in the Europe-Latina segment at only 8.8% due to what management calls "strukturlella utmaningar" and issues with gold handling, though they find the explanations unclear. The company is working on improvements and has growing Safe Point services. The hosts believe Loomis can reach 11.5% EBITDA margin and 5% annual growth, leading to 28 SEK per share earnings. At current levels (292 SEK) this represents P10, which they think is too low for a stable business - P14 is more reasonable. They have bought shares after Q4 report.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Istället för en omsättning på 5 miljarder till 2025, som var där man gick ut med från början, det är ju helt galet. Har de reviderat målsättningen till break even för Loomis Pay till 2026-2027 någonstans?

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Om man vågar tro att koncernen kan nå 11,5% ebitda marginal och växa med 5% per år framåt då ska de kunna tjäna 28 kronor per aktie kommande år. Det ger ett p på 10 då på aktuell kurs ungefär. Vi tycker att p14 kan vara mer rimligt för Loomis.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Väldigt lågt. För har inte de haft 16-17 i snitt på de sista tiondena?

stock_segments.discussion_summary: The hosts discuss Proact's Q1 report which showed revenue close to expectations but significantly better profitability than expected, leading to a strong stock rise. System revenues decreased 9% while service revenues increased 6%, with services now representing 46% of total revenue. New managed services contracts signed for 183 million SEK, up from 117 million last year. Recurring revenues increased 10% and are now at 1.8 billion SEK run-rate. EBIT was up 87% and earnings per share up 120%, which the hosts find surprising given no one-off items. They believe this may be an outlier and expect lower margins for the rest of the year. The company has strong balance sheet with net cash again and hasn't made an acquisition in almost 2 years. The hosts estimate 9 SEK EPS for full year, trading at P14 vs historical P17 average over 7 years. They believe P14 is too low given increasing stability from higher recurring revenues and strong historical performance. Insider purchases seen after report. The hosts continue to hold.

quotes.text: EBIT här i kvartalet upp 87 procent... Vinst per aktie upp 120 procent, hur det var... Vi låg långt under här.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Vi tror faktiskt att börsen har haft lite svårt med Proact, historiskt just för att systemetäkterna har varit en del upp och ner. Så det blir liksom jobbigt att pronosticera och man orkar inte se dem där.

quotes.text: P17 som de har värderats i det historiskt känns rimligt. Så P14 tycker vi fortfarande känns som faktiskt lite för lågt, om jag ska vara ärlig.

stock_segments.discussion_summary: The hosts provide an update on Securitas Q1 report, which they discussed in episode 164 when they bought a monitoring position. They have since increased to full holding. Q1 report met expectations with 4% revenue growth (7% organic) and EBITDA margin improving according to plan. However, weaker financial net meant EPS was 10% below hopes. Analysts expect 10 SEK per share for 2024 and 11.50 SEK for 2025, which the hosts stand behind. The stock trades at P11 for 2024 and P9.6 for 2025, which they consider very low for a profitable, stable company. Historical P15 is more reasonable in their view. Direct dividend yield ~10.5%. Main issue is weak European operations with only 5% operating margin vs 8.6% in USA, particularly at airport contracts where staffing difficulties have led to expensive overtime and contractors. Management is confident in reaching 8% operating margin target by end of 2025, even if it means lower growth (they've already cancelled a low-margin US airport contract for 1.6 billion SEK). Debt level is slightly below target of 3x net debt/EBITDA. Short interest remains at 9%. The hosts are confident in management improving European margins.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Med de siffrorna jag nyss sa då, 10 spänn, 24 och 11,50 för 2025, så handlas bolaget nu till P11 i år. Och P9,6 på 2025. Oerhört lågt för att vara sekuritas också.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Vi konstaterar att vi också förra gången vi tog upp sekuritas, att P15 är mer rimligt för ett tryggt lönsamt sekuritas som borde passa in bra i många långa portföljer.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: Vi har ingen anledning att inte tro på företagsledningen när de säger att de ser ljusare på marginalutvecklingen i Europa framåt.

stock_segments.discussion_summary: The hosts discuss Veteranpoolen Q1 report after taking it up in episode 157 at 30 SEK. The stock has since risen to 38 SEK (+27%). Q1 showed continued growth with 11% increase in worked hours, but profitability was weak with only 1.5% margin. The company cites establishment costs in Denmark (0.7 million SEK) and a provision for a dispute with a digital advertising supplier where the company ordered 0.7 million SEK of ads but supplier claims 4.3 million SEK, so they made a 0.75 million SEK provision. Adjusted margin was 2.9%, in line with last year but still weak. Revenue breakdown: care and home help developing well, handicraft weaker due to market conditions, and surprisingly good garden performance despite winter weather. On trailing 12 months, EPS is 2.03 SEK, PE 18.7 at 38 SEK stock price. The hosts expect EPS growth to 2.29 SEK in next 12 months, giving forward PE 16.5. April monthly report showed 21% growth, highest since August 2022. ROT-tax credit covering many of their jobs from July 2024 could help. Strong spring expected for garden and handicraft segments. Stock trades ex-dividend May 24 with dividend around 2 SEK (5% yield). The hosts continue to hold a small watch position, finding valuation reasonable but not yet compelling enough for full position.

quotes.speaker: Hosts
quotes.text: På rullande 12, om vi kollar värderingen, har man en vinstpax på 2,03. Aktiekurs 38 kronor, PE 18,7. Vi tror på vinstökning kommande 12 månader. Vi har ju varit ark 2,29, 16,5 i PE.

summary: The hosts discuss several Swedish stocks following the end of earnings season. Main themes include: the dramatic rise of Bergman & Beving from P10 to P39 as it moved into the "fine series" trading company segment, Loomis facing challenges in Europe but offering attractive value at P10, Proact's surprisingly strong Q1 report with improved margins making P14 valuation attractive, and Securitas trading at very low multiples (P11/P9.6) with confidence in margin improvements. They also discuss Revolution Race where Peter from Kavalier sees buying opportunities if major owners sell shares. Throughout, there's recognition of the hosts' tendency to sell too early and the challenge of market timing versus buy and hold strategies.
key_takeaways: Bergman & Beving soared to P39 from P10 as market re-rated it into quality trading company segment
Loomis trades at attractive P10 with potential for margin improvement and 4.5% dividend yield
Proact's Q1 showed surprising profitability with EBIT up 87%, making P14 valuation too low vs historical P17
Securitas very cheap at P11/P9.6 with confidence in reaching 8% operating margin by end of 2025
Revolution Race presents buying opportunities if Altor and Nyrenstein sell more shares according to Kavalier
Market is broadly bullish with rally across stocks, commodities and crypto
Hosts acknowledge pattern of selling too early with stocks like AQ, VBG and Bergman & Beving performing better after sale
